assignment.review_focus: Perform a cross-finding synthesis and escalation assessment across all completed agent runs (RUN-0002 through RUN-0006) to support final report assembly. Specifically: (1) Assess whether the IFT-prefixed document number on the active Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 vs. expected PT9L-FXJH01) constitutes a document-control nonconformance under the applicable SOP or whether it is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. (2) Assess whether the F0013 PT2L risk plan carrying a PT9L-series document number internally (identified by both Risk Traceability Agent and Regulatory Agent) represents a single root cause or two distinct nonconformances requiring separate corrective actions. (3) Assess whether the biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples are covered by any equivalence or shared-component justification in the DHF, or whether this constitutes an unmitigated gap for 510(k) and CE submissions. (4) Assess whether the operation guide reference to MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance is a live document in the controlled release set or a draft/historical artifact. (5) Identify any findings across all agent runs that, in combination, suggest a systemic document-control process failure (e.g., unsigned approvals appearing across risk, design output, and DMR documents simultaneously) that should be flagged as a systemic finding rather than individual point findings. (6) Confirm whether the dual ASTM E1965 version citation (1998:2016 and 1998:2023) appears in the same document or in different documents at different design stages, and whether any transition rationale document exists in the corpus.

assignment.review_focus: Perform a cross-finding synthesis and escalation assessment across all completed agent runs (RUN-0002 through RUN-0006) to support final report assembly. Specifically: (1) Assess whether the IFT-prefixed document number on the active Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 vs. expected PT9L-FXJH01) constitutes a document-control nonconformance under the applicable SOP or whether it is a known legacy prefix with a documented transition record. agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

findings.claim: Unsigned approval fields appear simultaneously across all active risk management documents, all historical risk management documents, and the design output list, constituting a systemic document-control process failure rather than isolated point deficiencies.
findings.rationale: Every risk management document in the active PT9L set carries a blank 'Approved by (Technical Director) Date:' field: F0017 (REG-015), F0018 (REG-019), F0019 (REG-024), F0020 (REG-027), F0021 (REG-031), F0022 (REG-035), F0023 (REG-040), F0024 (REG-043). The same pattern is present in all historical-folder documents: F0012 (REG-001), F0013 (REG-003), F0014 (REG-006), F0015 (REG-012), F0016 (REG-013), F0025 (REG-046), F0026 (REG-048), F0027 (REG-054), F0028 (REG-056). RUN-0005 independently identified blank approval-date fields in the design output list. RUN-0007 confirmed no signed pass verdict is present in the battery verification record. The simultaneous absence of completed approval signatures across risk management, design output, and verification documents spanning multiple product variants and multiple document versions indicates that the document-control SOP governing approval capture is either not being enforced or is not functioning. This cannot be attributed to a single document author or a single review cycle; it is a process-level gap requiring a corrective action at the SOP and training level, not merely document-by-document remediation.
challenge_questions: Can the manufacturer produce a document-control SOP that specifies the required approval workflow, and can it demonstrate that this SOP was in effect during the periods when these documents were created or revised?

Is there a separate wet-ink or electronic signature record maintained outside the document body that constitutes the formal approval record for these files? If so, where is it stored and how is it linked to each document version?

Has a root-cause analysis been performed to determine why approval fields are blank across documents spanning at least two product variants (PT9L and PT2L) and at least two version cycles (V1.0 and V2.0)?
What corrective action has been or will be taken at the process level, beyond retroactively completing individual approval fields?

findings.claim: F0013 (PT2L risk management plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number, representing two distinct nonconformances—a product-identity mismatch and a document-number assignment error—that share a single root cause but require separate corrective actions.
findings.rationale: REG-003 and REG-004 show F0013 is filed as a PT2L risk management plan (path: '03 风险分析\2L风险改 - 历史文件\V1.0-1 Risk Management Plan PT2L美亚-FXJH01 V1.0') yet the document internally carries the identifier FXJH01 which is the same functional suffix as the PT9L Risk Management Plan (IFT-FXJH01 / PT9L-FXJH01). The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 2) asks whether this is one root cause or two distinct nonconformances. Assessment: the root cause is likely a copy-paste or template-reuse error during document creation, but the resulting nonconformances are distinct: (a) a product-identity nonconformance—a PT2L product document contains PT9L-series numbering, creating ambiguity about which product's risk file is authoritative; and (b) a document-number assignment nonconformance—the same functional document number suffix (FXJH01) is assigned to risk management plans for two different products without a documented shared-document or family-document justification. These require separate corrective actions because (a) requires a product-scope clarification and possible re-issuance of the PT2L document under a PT2L-specific number, while (b) requires a document-number registry review to ensure no other cross-product number collisions exist.
challenge_questions: Was F0013 intentionally created as a PT2L-specific document, or was it intended to be a shared risk management plan covering both PT2L and PT9L under a family approach? If the latter, where is the family-device justification?
Has a document-number collision check been performed across all products in the PT9L product family to identify other instances where the same document-number suffix is used for different products?
What is the disposition of F0013 in the current PT9L DHF—is it referenced as supporting evidence, as a historical artifact, or as an active controlled document?

findings.claim: Biocompatibility testing was conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L samples, and no equivalence justification, shared-component declaration, or bridging rationale document was found in the supplied corpus, leaving an unmitigated gap for both 510(k) and CE submissions.
findings.rationale: F0104–F0108 (REG-088 through REG-116) are all filed under the path '11 T1样机\生物相容性\同PT5生物相容性报告\' and are explicitly titled with 'PT5' sample identifiers. The operation guide (F0083, REG-074) states that patient-contact materials (ABS, TPU, PMMA, PC) have passed ISO 10993-5 and ISO 10993-10 tests, but does not identify the test samples as PT9L. The orchestrator's escalation question (ASG-0008 item 3) asks whether any equivalence or shared-component justification exists in the DHF. No such document appears in the evidence catalog. For a 510(k) submission, FDA expects biocompatibility testing to be conducted on the actual device or a documented equivalent; a bridging memo citing identical materials, identical suppliers, and identical manufacturing processes would be required. For CE under MDR 2017/745, Annex I Chapter II requires biocompatibility evaluation of the actual device. The absence of any bridging or equivalence record in the corpus means this gap is currently unmitigated.
challenge_questions: Is there a biocompatibility equivalence memo or shared-component declaration that documents that PT5 and PT9L use identical patient-contact materials from identical suppliers with identical manufacturing processes? If so, in which controlled document is it maintained and what is its document number?
Were the PT5 biocompatibility tests conducted on the same material grades and formulations as those specified in the PT9L BOM and material specifications?
Has the 510(k) submission package included a biocompatibility bridging rationale, and has FDA accepted it? Has the CE technical file addressed this under MDR Annex I Chapter II?

Does the CE technical file for PT9L reference this operation guide, and if so, has the notified body or EU authorized representative been notified of the incorrect regulatory citation?
